Subject: Acme RAG eval - post-call next steps

Hi Sam - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can get a focused POC running: 

Call recap:
- Goal: Improve answer grounding and reduce hallucinations for internal product docs + API spec queries. Primary success metric: grounding precision >= 95% on in-scope queries; secondary: median latency < 400ms for single-document responses.
- Data: ~120k technical docs (PDFs + markdown), S3-hosted, 30GB compressed.
- Key constraints: PII redaction, retention policy = 90 days, customer-managed KMS required.

Our recommended initial approach (quick summary):
1) Retriever: hybrid dense + sparse (FAISS/HNSW + BM25) for high recall on technical terms. Start with dense-only if you prefer simpler infra.
2) Retriever params we suggest for the POC: dense nprobe/k equivalent -> retrieve 50 candidates; BM25 top 50; merge and dedupe.
3) Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for top-10 (recommended model: redwood-rerank-cross-3b). This gives a large boost to grounding precision with modest cost increase.
4) Generator models (for final answer generation):
   - Cost-sensitive option: redwood-compat-7b-q4 + cross-encoder reranker (good balance of cost/quality).
   - High-precision option: redwood-compat-13b-q4 + reranker (best grounding, slightly higher latency/cost).
5) Prompt sets & evals: attached is an initial prompt_set + a short eval summary from our internal sandbox showing baseline retrieval recall / grounding rates. Please review and share a small representative query set if you have one.

Suggested POC plan / timeline:
- Week 0: Access & data ingest (we'll need a read-only S3 role or secure upload).
- Week 1: Indexing & baseline retrieval configs (dense index + BM25).
- Week 2: Reranker + initial model runs on your sample queries.
- Week 3: Shared eval and tuning; decision point on Dedicated vs Hosted.

Ask from you:
- Confirm who will provide the sample query set (10-50 queries covering difficult cases).
- Confirm S3 access method (IAM role or temporary upload).
- Any constraints on model family (open-source only / no external endpoints)?

Attached: acme_rag_prompt_set_v1.json, acme_eval_summary_QR.csv

I can put Marcus on the thread to handle indexing/tuning; cc'd. If that looks good, I'll send a calendar invite for a kickoff next week.

Best,

Sam - good questions, answers below and a few links.

1) Image/PDF handling: Redwood's ingestion pipeline supports OCR as part of the ingest (we run Tesseract/OCROps as a step). For POCs we can either ingest your OCRed text or run the OCR pipeline; if you prefer we can run OCR in your VPC during ingestion (private deploy option).

2) Realistic grounding expectations: for technical corpora with high-quality retrieval + cross-encoder reranker + 13b generator we've seen grounding precision in the 92-97% range on benchmarked sets. For domain-specific API docs it depends on tokenization and how often answers are verbatim in the corpus. Our suggested rollout is: start with 7b-q4 + reranker to establish baseline and then run the 13b-q4 as a controlled comparison. We'll run our standard eval harness measuring: grounding precision (support precision), support recall, MRR@10, and hallucination rate (false_positive_answer_rate).

3) Pricing (rough POC estimates):
- Hosted (ephemeral capacity for 3 weeks of POC): ~$6k-10k (indexing + 10k gen tokens/day + reranker runs).
- Dedicated reserved (1 month minimum): starting ~$18k/month depending on capacity and SLA.
I'll have a more detailed line-item after Marcus scopes the indexing/compute needs.

Useful links:
- POC benchmark & example prompts: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-rag
- HubSpot record: HS-12345
- Shared drive with prompt set & eval: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-acme-rag-eval
